title: Snowbirds bid farewell to legendary jets in final flight over Calgary

blocks.text: Calgary·New

The legendary CT-114 Tutor jets of the Canadian Forces Snowbirds took to the skies one last time over Calgary's McMahon Stadium Nov. 15, 2026, right before the 113th Grey Cup kicked off, setting the stage for a dynamic match between the Edmonton Elks and Montreal Alouettes.
CT-114 Tutor jets flew over McMahon Stadium for Grey Cup
The legendary jets of the Canadian Forces Snowbirds took to the skies one last time Sunday evening.

Smoke trailed behind the team's signature red-and-white CT-114 Tutor jets as they roared over Calgary's McMahon Stadium right before the 113th Grey Cup kicked off, setting the stage for a dynamic match between the Edmonton Elks and Montreal Alouettes.
In an interview with CBC News before the flight, Capt. Patrick Charette reflected on his time with the Snowbirds.
"Every good thing comes to an end," he said.
The Canadian Forces Snowbirds' CT-114 Tutor jets took to the skies one last time over Calgary's McMahon Stadium Nov. 15, 2026. (Amir Said/CBC)
The federal government announced in May that the CT-114 Tutor jets, which the CAF ordered as training aircraft in 1961, would be retired after the 2026 flying season.
"This is the end of this chapter for the Snowbirds, but we're proud and happy to be here in front of as many Canadians as posible, and we're excited for the future," Charette said.
Capt. Patrick Charette pictured in a file photo. This is his second season as a pilot with the Canadian Forces Snowbirds. (Cory Herperger/Radio-Canada)
The jets are set to be replaced by Swiss-made CT-157 Siskin II planes, but those won't be here until the 2030s at the earliest.
"We're excited for the future, coming back in a few years with the new aircraft and new team," Charette said.
"I can't imagine a more fitting occasion to do our last public display than the Grey Cup here in Calgary," he said

blocks.text: Aviation enthusiasts gathered across northwest Calgary to witness the squadron's last Tutor flyover.

"It's the only time I've really gotten to get a good look at them," said Ben Hunt, one of several plane spotters who gathered at the University of Calgary to watch the jets take their historic final flight.
"It's sad to see them go," he said.
The final flight of the Canadian Forces Snowbirds' CT-114 Tutor jets photographed from the University of Calgary on Nov. 15, 2026. (Michael King/CBC)
It was Jaime Garcia's third time seeing the Snowbirds in action.
"This is the last time unfortunately," he said. "Hopefully they come back stronger in a few years."
The Canadian Forces Snowbirds' CT-114 Tutor jets trailed their signature smoke as they roared over Calgary's McMahon Stadium for their last flight on Nov. 15, 2026. (Amir Said/CBC)
Garcia, an engineer who immigrated from Mexico, says the Snowbirds serve as an inspiration.
"Seeing them perform their tricks, and just seeing the skill and the talent of Canadian pilots, it inspires me," he said. "It makes me very happy to be in this country."
